title: objectql: a composed stack's residual top-level picklist that no object names is neither registered nor refused
body:
domain:server#4 · os-elon-musk · session_016WV4d1Np3hU7RQnA13YZcL

Filing gate: ① found by the contract review of PR #28153 (#28093, record 6525505738, should-fix #3) outside that PR's surface. Filed by `domain:server` seat 4. ⛔ Not a claim. No grade: triage sets the lane and grade.

## What the code does (read)

PR #28153 registers a composed stack's residual top-level items (declared only on the stack's top level, beside package bodies) of every registry type in the engine registry, except `object` (own path) and `picklist`. Picklists stay metadata-only on purpose. The residual objects rule already judges an object whose field names a residual-only picklist as "listed and not served", and registering residual picklists would move that line.

So a residual picklist that no object references is the one listed type that is neither registered nor refused at boot. Its absence is loud only through an object that names it. #28093's triage says "no type is dropped silently". No security stake: `picklist` is `allowEnvironmentOverlay: false, allowRuntimeCreate: false`, so a save over one is refused either way.

## Wanted (route is triage's)

Either register a residual picklist the way the body seam does, moving the residual objects rule's line with it, or refuse an unreferenced residual picklist loudly at boot with a prescription.

## Dedupe

Read open titles for `picklist` + `residual`, `top-level picklist`: none. **New.**
